# Feature: Shape-Aware Extraction with Links

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-051
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_task_fidelity.md` (G2, G3; §5 "Changed tool contracts"; §6 "discovered links turn page content into navigation authority" and "structured data is untrusted input"; §7 "Two shapes of evidence", "Collection extraction, stated so it cannot become site logic", "Evidence identity has one owner", and the target trace; §8; §9; §11 "Turns spent seeking unreachable URLs"; §13 TODO lines 208, 210, 214)

Make every page read report what kind of page it is and return the data that kind of page actually holds. Listings come back as records, product and vehicle pages as label/value fields, data pages as all of their tables, and schema.org markup as structured entities. Every read also returns the links a page offers, and those links become navigable because the page attested them.

Run `20260925T130634Z-research-e1fd1b9d` shows both halves of the gap:

- **G2.** `web_fetch` of a results page returned 2,302 bytes: facet labels followed by bare price blocks. The card titles and seller names in the same cards were dropped. [`ReadabilityExtractor`](../../../packages/core/src/extraction/readability.ts#L53-L88) removes `nav`, `aside`, and `form` before running Readability, and Readability is built to discard link-dense repeated blocks, which is where a collection keeps its records. The browser path is no better:
  - `browser_extract` `content` collapses `innerText` onto one line ([`agent-controller.ts:1140-1144`](../../../packages/core/src/browser/agent-controller.ts#L1140-L1144)).
  - `table` reads only the first `<table>` ([`agent-controller.ts:1146-1157`](../../../packages/core/src/browser/agent-controller.ts#L1146-L1157)).
  - JSON-LD is read only for `datePublished` ([`readability.ts:112-127`](../../../packages/core/src/extraction/readability.ts#L112-L127)).

  The agent could not see why fields were missing, so it published an invented cause ("renders client-side") as fact.

- **G3.** `web_fetch` tells the model to fetch "a link discovered inside previously fetched content" ([`web-fetch.ts:51-52`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-fetch.ts#L51-L52)), but its result contains no links ([`web-fetch.ts:192-202`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-fetch.ts#L192-L202)). Pagination, facet filters, and detail pages were unreachable by construction. The model spent 14 of its 15 turns trying to reach them. Meanwhile `web_fetch` itself accepts any URL, including a hand-assembled one ([TODO line 208](../../TODO.md)).

Acceptance requires all of the following:

- Every successful `web_fetch` reports a `shape`: `article`, `collection`, `table`, `detail`, or `index`. It also carries a `coverage` statement saying what extraction found, what it showed, what it dropped, and what it looked for and did not find.
- **Article pages are unchanged.** For every page today's extractor reads as an article, `text` is byte-identical to today's output. This is pinned by FEAT-049's `article` golden file and by core fixtures.
- **Collection pages** return up to 25 `records`, each with an anchor `S<n>#r<k>`, a title, a primary link, ordered text segments, label/value fields, and typed numeric tokens. A card whose title and seller are links and whose price is plain text yields a record that contains the seller (the G2 regression, plan §9).
- Facet lists are returned as `facet` links, never as records. Pagination is returned as `pagination` links.
- Schema.org JSON-LD and microdata entities of an allowlisted `@type` are returned as `structured[]`. They are bounded by bytes, depth, and count. A page whose only data is an `ItemList` of products is a `collection`.
- **Tables.** Every `<table>` is reachable by its document-order index. `web_fetch` returns `tables[]`, and `browser_extract` accepts `kind: "tables"` or `kind: "table", index: n`.
- **Links.** At most 40 links per page, deduplicated, ranked by kind and then same-site first. `javascript:`, `data:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, and same-document links are dropped. A link is offered only when the public sanitizer leaves it byte-identical, so the URL the model copies is exactly the URL that was recorded.
- **Provenance.** Every URL a result shows the model (links, record URLs, structured URL properties, and URLs written in returned text) is recorded into `UrlProvenance` as `discovered`, naming the containing source. `web_fetch` now refuses unattested URLs with `URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE`, exactly as `browser_navigate` does today. Every `web_fetch` and `browser_navigate` audit record states how its URL was attested.
- `web_search` sites carry a compact shape summary. A later `web_fetch` of that URL returns the full view from the run document store, with no network fetch and no navigation charged.
- `browser_extract` gains `records`, `links`, `structured`, and `tables`. `content` keeps block structure. Every kind runs through the **same** core analyzer as `web_fetch`, over a serialized snapshot of the live page.
- Shape classification and record detection reuse the extractor's existing cheerio parse. They add **zero** HTML parses on the `web_fetch` path, asserted by a parse counter.
- No module under `extraction/page/` reads a `class` or `id` attribute, names a host, or branches on a URL literal. A boundary test enforces this.
- FEAT-049's deterministic tier passes with `FEAT-051` removed from `PENDING_OWNERS`.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope: G2 and G3 in full, TODO lines 208 and 214, and the extraction half of line 210 (the new `browser_extract` kinds feed the ledger).

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:

- The run document store, `S<n>` minting, `already_read`, `limit: 0` discovery, the budget meter, and the response classifier (**FEAT-050**). FEAT-051 adds page payloads and record anchors to the store, and consumes `classifyResponse`.
- Typed failure codes, notices, and `RunHealth` itself (**FEAT-048**). FEAT-051 adds one optional `extraction` block.
- Research browsing, the task contract, and prompt `agent-v9` (**FEAT-052**). FEAT-051 changes tool descriptions only.
- Citing `S<n>#r<k>` in the Brief, `row_citations`, and the anchoring check (**FEAT-053**). FEAT-051 provides `documents.resolveAnchor()` for it.
- The deterministic `ask` and `research --no-llm` pipelines. They keep calling `extractor.extract()`, which is byte-identical to today (plan §7).
- `browser_observe`'s digest stays on Readability, and observing a page still records no evidence (TODO line 210, second half).
- Script-only filters, "load more" buttons, and checkbox facets inside forms. These belong to `do` (plan §7, "Why research gets read-only browsing").

### Deviations from the plan (flagged, awaiting confirmation)

1. **DEVIATION: `challenge` is never a success shape.** Plan §5 lists `challenge` among `shape` values. FEAT-050 already makes a challenge page a `SITE_CHALLENGE` failure on `web_fetch` and `web_search`, because a challenge page must never be extracted. FEAT-051 extends the same failure to `browser_extract` (TASK-008). A success result that said "shape: challenge" would contradict that rule. `PageShape` therefore excludes it.
2. **DEVIATION: a fifth shape, `index`.** A page with no readable content, records, tables, fields, or structured data, but with followable links (a hub, landing, or category page), is today an `EXTRACTION_EMPTY` failure. A failure's `details` are not model-visible, so the links would be lost, which is exactly G3. FEAT-051 returns it as a success with `shape: "index"` and `links[]`. Pages with no links either stay `EXTRACTION_EMPTY`.
3. **Clarification, not a deviation: `web_fetch` gains a provenance gate.** Plan §5 says hand-assembled URLs are "refused exactly as today". That is true of `browser_navigate`, but `web_fetch` accepts any URL today (TODO line 208; FEAT-049 pins the acceptance as a baseline). Plan §6 ("Hand-assembled URLs remain refused. This closes the laundering path TODO line 208 describes") requires the gate, so TASK-005 adds it.
4. **Supersedes a FEAT-050 rule.** FEAT-050 TASK-003 says a `table` extraction mints no source by itself. Plan §13 (line 210) says FEAT-051's extract kinds feed the ledger. Under FEAT-051, every `browser_extract` kind except `links` records evidence (TASK-008).

#### Implementation deviations (recorded by Implement, 2026-10-12)

5. **DEVIATION: `detail` mass floors each field at `FIELD_FACT_CHARS` (60).** §2 says detail mass is "field text". On FEAT-049's own faceted detail page (8 attributes, two boilerplate paragraphs), raw field text (129 chars) lost to the article reading, so a detail page read as an article. A label/value pair states one fact that prose spends a sentence on, so each pair now counts as at least 60 characters (`shape.ts`). The article-with-infobox and comment-thread fixtures still read as articles.
6. **DEVIATION: article mass counts only unexplained prose.** The article reading's mass is Readability's text minus the pieces other parts already return (record text, field labels/values, table cells, offered link labels), counted as letter/digit runs, × `ARTICLE_MASS_WEIGHT`. An article with no prose of its own does not qualify. Without this, a hub whose Readability text is only its link labels could never be `index`, and under the raw formula `multi-table` lost to the article reading, 230 to 246. `shape_basis` reports both numbers.
7. **DEVIATION: facet groups need 2 items, not `MIN_RECORDS`.** FEAT-049's facet sidebar offers two-value groups (new/used, AWD/FWD), and §2's candidate rule (≥ 3 children) would never see them, so the AWD facet target was unreachable. `FACET_MIN_ITEMS = 2`. Each item must still pass all three facet tests, and a label must accompany the count, so a numbered page list is never a facet group. An anchor to the page itself (the selected value) counts toward its group.
8. **DEVIATION: `coverage.omitted` is data in core, rendered by the agent.** Core emits `{ id, count, table?, paginationOffered? }`, and `projectPage` renders each through the registered message catalog. TASK-006 requires the omitted phrases to be registered templates that declare their capabilities, and core cannot import the agent's registry. The model still sees `coverage.omitted: string[]`.
9. **Clarification: `analyzePage` is two phases.** `analyzePage($, { baseUrl, fetchMode })` scans the untouched parse, and `completeAnalysis(scan, { articleText, fallbackText })` folds in Readability and decides the shape. Analysis must run before the pre-clean, and the article is known only after it.
10. **Clarification: the `not_found` phrase is "no structured data".** §2's example "no schema.org data" matches the boundary test's own hostname-literal rule.
11. **Clarification: a page with only sub-threshold parts is not empty.** A page with no qualifying reading but a non-layout table, or fields/entities, reads as `table` or `detail` before `index` is considered. Only a page with no article and no page parts is `EXTRACTION_EMPTY`.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No relational store, and `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. Everything here is either in-memory run state or a tool payload, plus one additive optional block on FEAT-048's `RunHealth`.

### Core analysis types (`packages/core/src/extraction/page/types.ts`)

- **`PageShape`**: `'article' | 'collection' | 'table' | 'detail' | 'index'`.
- **`LinkKind`**: `'pagination' | 'facet' | 'record' | 'content' | 'navigation'`.
  - `pagination` and `facet` follow the structural rules in TASK-001 and TASK-002.
  - `record` is the primary link of a record.
  - `navigation` is any other link inside a `nav`, `header`, `footer`, or `aside` landmark, or inside `role=navigation|banner|contentinfo|complementary`.
  - `content` is everything else.
- **`PageLink`**: `{ text: string (≤ 80 chars; falls back to aria-label, title, then img alt), url: string (absolute, http/https), kind: LinkKind, sameSite: boolean }`.
- **`NumericToken`**: `{ kind: 'currency' | 'distance' | 'count'; text: string; value: number }`. `text` is the matched span. `value` is parsed, with grouping separators removed.
- **`PageRecord`**:
  - `key: string`: the identity used for stable anchors (TASK-006). It is the canonical primary URL when one exists; otherwise a hash of the normalized title plus the first segment.
  - `title: string | null`: the first `h1`–`h6` in the record, else the primary link's text, else the first segment.
  - `url: string | null`: the primary link. That is the anchor wrapping or nearest the title, else the anchor with the longest text.
  - `segments: string[]`: the record's visible block-level text runs in document order, de-duplicated, title excluded.
  - `fields: { label: string; value: string }[]`: at most 8 pairs, from `dt`/`dd`, in-record `th`/`td`, and "Label: value" segments.
  - `numbers: NumericToken[]`: at most 6.
  - `links: { text: string; url: string }[]`: at most 3 secondary links in the record, such as a seller link.
  - **Bound:** at most 400 characters across title, segments, and field values. Overflow is cut at a segment boundary and counted.
- **`StructuredEntity`**: `{ type: string; from: 'json-ld' | 'microdata'; props: Record<string, string | number | boolean> }`.
  - `props` flattens nested objects to dotted keys (`offers.price`, `offers.seller.name`) and indexes arrays of objects (`offers.0.price`).
  - Limits: nesting depth 4, at most 40 properties, strings at most 300 characters, and at most 2 KB serialized per entity.
- **`PageTable`**:
  - `index: number`: the 0-based document-order ordinal among **all** `<table>` elements on the page, nested ones included, in pre-order. It equals the array position and the `browser_extract` `index`.
  - `kind`: `'data' | 'key-value' | 'layout'`.
  - `caption: string | null`, `headers: string[]`, `rows: string[][]`.
  - Limits: at most 50 rows and 20 columns, and cells of at most 200 characters.
  - A `layout` table (a single cell, or one that contains a nested table) has `rows: []`.
- **`PageCoverage`**:
  - `shape_basis: string`: one sentence saying why the shape won, for example "collection: 24 repeated records (5,210 chars) outweighed article text (2,302 chars)".
  - `fetch_mode: 'http' | 'browser'`.
  - `records?: { found, shown, with_link, with_fields }`.
  - `links?: { found, shown, withheld, by_kind: Partial<Record<LinkKind, number>> }`.
  - `tables?: { found, shown }`.
  - `structured?: { found, shown, types: string[], ignored_types: string[] }`.
  - `fields?: { found, shown }`.
  - `text?: { chars, shown }`.
  - `not_found: string[]`: fixed phrases for what was looked for and absent, such as "no repeated records", "no schema.org data", "no tables", or "no label/value fields".
  - `omitted: string[]`: one fixed phrase per bound that dropped data. Each phrase names an engineered way to get the rest, or says plainly that there is none.
- **`PageAnalysis`**: `{ shape, records: PageRecord[] (≤ 25), structured: StructuredEntity[] (≤ 25), tables: PageTable[] (≤ 10), fields: { label, value }[] (≤ 60), links: PageLink[] (≤ 40, record links excluded), recordLinkCount: number, readableText: string, coverage: PageCoverage }`.
  - `readableText` is Readability's `contentText` when an article exists. Otherwise it is the body's visible text, block-structured through the existing `htmlToText`/`normalizeExtractedText` pass.
- **`PageExtraction`**: `{ article: ExtractedArticle | null; page: PageAnalysis }`.
- **`PageExtractor extends Extractor`**: adds `extractPage(doc: FetchedDoc): Promise<PageExtraction>`. `ReadabilityExtractor` implements it. `extract()` is unchanged and runs no analysis.
- **`PageSnapshot`** (core, `browser/types.ts`): `{ url: string; title: string; html: string; visibleText: string; truncated: boolean }`. `html` is `document.documentElement.outerHTML`, capped at the same byte limit the HTTP fetcher enforces. `truncated` is `true` when the cap cut it.

Named constants, each in the module that uses it with a one-line rationale:

| Constant              | Value   | Applies to                                               |
| --------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MAX_RECORDS`         | 25      | records shown per page                                   |
| `RECORD_TEXT_CHARS`   | 400     | text per record                                          |
| `MIN_RECORDS`         | 3       | records needed for a collection                          |
| `SIBLING_SIMILARITY`  | 0.6     | Jaccard similarity for sibling records                   |
| `RECORD_MIN_TEXT`     | 20      | characters a record must hold                            |
| `LANDMARK_PENALTY`    | 0.2     | score multiplier inside landmarks                        |
| `MAX_LINKS`           | 40      | links per page                                           |
| `FACET_LABEL_MAX`     | 60      | characters in a facet label                              |
| `MAX_TABLES`          | 10      | tables per page                                          |
| `MAX_TABLE_ROWS`      | 50      | rows per table                                           |
| `MAX_TABLE_COLS`      | 20      | columns per table                                        |
| `CELL_CHARS`          | 200     | characters per cell                                      |
| `MAX_FIELDS`          | 60      | page-level label/value pairs                             |
| `LABEL_MAX`           | 40      | characters in a field label                              |
| `VALUE_MAX`           | 200     | characters in a field value                              |
| `JSONLD_SCRIPT_BYTES` | 256 KiB | bytes read from one JSON-LD script                       |
| `JSONLD_TOTAL_BYTES`  | 1 MiB   | bytes read across all JSON-LD scripts                    |
| `STRUCTURED_DEPTH`    | 6       | parse depth (flattening stops at 4)                      |
| `MAX_STRUCTURED`      | 25      | structured entities shown                                |
| `ARTICLE_MASS_WEIGHT` | 0.5     | discount on article text in shape arbitration (TASK-004) |

### Agent-side model payload (`packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/page-payload.ts`)

- **`projectPage(input, view, budgetBytes, services)`** builds the model-visible object for one page from a `StoredPage` (below), the `sourceId`, and a view:
  - **`'full'`**: used by `web_fetch` and `browser_extract`. Fields: `source_id`, `url`, `title`, `shape`, and the primary part for the shape. That is `records` for `collection`, `tables` for `table`, `fields` for `detail`, `text` for `article`, and `links` for `index`. Then come the secondary parts in the fixed order `fields`, `tables`, `structured`, `records`, `links`, then `text` (or `excerpt` plus `capture_ref`), then `coverage`. `byline` and `published_at` are added when the shape is `article`.
  - **`'summary'`**: used by `web_search` sites. Fields: `source_id`, `url`, `title`, `shape`, at most 5 records, at most 10 `pagination`/`facet` links, the excerpt, `coverage`, and a `note` from the registered message `page-summary`. The note says that a `web_fetch` of this URL returns the full view from this run's store without a new fetch.
  - **Degradation.** `projectPage` serializes the candidate and measures UTF-8 bytes. It degrades deterministically until the object fits `budgetBytes`:
    1. `text` → `excerpt` (1,000 characters) plus `capture_ref` (the existing `writeCapture`);
    2. trim `links` to 20, then 10;
    3. trim `structured`, then `tables` rows, then `records` from the end, one at a time.

    Every trim adds a phrase to `coverage.omitted`. The full `PageAnalysis` JSON is written once as a capture whenever anything was trimmed, so nothing is lost from the run directory.

  - The budget is `0.9 × maxBytesPerResult` for a full view. For a summary it is `floor(0.8 × maxBytesPerResult / fetchedSites)`. The 10% headroom absorbs sanitizer growth. The middleware's hard byte truncation stays as the last resort, and a test asserts that it never fires on the fixture corpus.

- Record wire form: `{ id: 'S3#r5', title, url, text: segments, fields: Record<label, value>, numbers: [{ kind, text }], links }`. When a label repeats, later copies get a ` (2)` suffix. Empty members are omitted.
- Structured wire form: `{ type, from, props }`. Table wire form: `{ index, kind, caption, headers, rows }`. Link wire form: `{ text, url, kind }`.
- **`offerableUrl(url, services)`** runs the URL through exactly the middleware's model-visible transform: the user-input mask, then the `public` sanitizer, exported from `middleware.ts` as `modelVisibleText(value, profile, services)` with no byte bounding. It returns `true` only when the output is byte-identical to the input. A link or record URL that fails is withheld, its `url` is set to `null`, and `coverage.links.withheld` counts it.

### Run document store extensions (FEAT-050's `DocumentStore`, additive)

- `DocumentRecord.page: StoredPage | null` (null until a shape-aware read attaches one). `StoredPage` = `{ analysis: PageAnalysis; anchors: Map<recordKey, k>; article: { byline, publishedAt } | null; delivered: 'full' | 'summary' }`.
- **`attachPage(sourceId, analysis, opts: { delivered; article })`** assigns anchors and stores the page, replacing any earlier analysis of the same source.
  - **Stable anchors.** A record whose `key` already has an anchor in this source keeps it. A new key gets `max(k) + 1`. Re-extracting a live page never renumbers a record that was already cited.
- **`markDelivered(sourceId, 'full')`**.
- **`resolveAnchor(id: string): { sourceId; record: PageRecord } | null`**. It parses `S<n>#r<k>` and returns `null` for malformed IDs and unknown sources or anchors. FEAT-053 consumes it.
- **Repeat-read rule** (changes FEAT-050's `hit` branch for `web_fetch` only):
  - When the record's `page.delivered === 'summary'`, `web_fetch` returns the **full** projection from the store with `from_store: true`, then marks it `full`. There is no network load, no `reserve`, no evidence re-add, and no rank signal.
  - Otherwise it returns FEAT-050's `already_read` payload unchanged.

### URL provenance extensions (`packages/agent/src/runtime/url-provenance.ts`)

- **`ProvenanceOrigin`** (discriminated union):
  - `{ kind: 'goal' }`
  - `{ kind: 'allow-host' }`
  - `{ kind: 'tool'; tool: string }` (search results, fetched URLs, browser results)
  - `{ kind: 'discovered'; sourceId: string; linkKind: LinkKind | 'text' | 'structured' }`
- `record(url, origin)`: `origin` is required, a clean break, and every call site is updated. The **first** origin for a normalized URL wins.
- **`explain(url): { match: 'exact' | 'origin-root' | 'query-variant' | 'allowed-host'; origin: ProvenanceOrigin } | null`**. It is the same decision as `has()`, which is now `explain(url) !== null`, so the two cannot diverge. For a non-exact match, `origin` is the origin of the recorded URL that granted it.

### Run health (protocol, additive, `schema_version` unchanged)

- `RunHealth.extraction?: { pages_by_shape: Partial<Record<PageShape, number>>; records_shown: number; links_offered: number; links_withheld: number; discovered_follows: number }`.
  - `discovered_follows` counts successful `web_fetch` and `browser_navigate` calls whose `explain().origin.kind === 'discovered'`. It is plan §11's "turns spent seeking unreachable URLs" measured from the other side.
  - Old run directories validate unchanged.

### Relationships

- `DocumentRecord` 1:0..1 `StoredPage`; `StoredPage` 1:N `PageRecord`, each with exactly one stable anchor `k`.
- `PageLink` N:1 `DocumentRecord` (the containing source), recorded as a `discovered` `ProvenanceOrigin` naming its `sourceId`.
- A provenance chain is reconstructable from the audit: each discovered hop's record names its `via` source, and that source's own fetch record names how its URL was attested.

### Indexes & Constraints

- Anchor `k` is unique per source, starts at 1, and is never reassigned within a run.
- `tables[i].index === i` for every shown table.
- `links` contains no two entries with the same `canonicalUrl` (FEAT-050's identity function) and never contains a record's primary URL when `records` is in the same payload.
- Every URL in a model payload is either offerable (byte-identical after the model-visible transform) or `null`.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

> **Running tests.** Per memory, `packages/agent`, `apps/cli`, and `e2e` resolve `@yantra/core` and `@yantra/protocol` from built `dist/`. Run `npx turbo run build --filter=@yantra/core --filter=@yantra/protocol` before trusting any non-core result. Targeted runs use `cd packages/<pkg> && npx vitest run <path>`. The repo-wide `npx turbo run lint typecheck` plus the `e2e` suite is the gate.

> **Fixture rule.** Every new HTML fixture encodes one nameable generic pattern ("listing cards with a linked seller line", "facet list with parenthesized counts"). Site names may appear only in a header provenance comment, and fixture bodies must stay clean against `SITE_TOKEN_SOURCE` (memory → never write website-specific logic).

### TASK-001: `extractPage` on one parse: shape skeleton, link harvest, and the structural-only boundary

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Extractor.** Refactor `ReadabilityExtractor`:
    - `parseHtml` is an injected seam that defaults to cheerio's `load`.
    - The private `readArticle($, doc)` holds today's pre-clean, `JSDOM`, Readability, and `htmlToText` code, moved verbatim.
    - `extract(doc)` = parse → `readArticle`, exactly as today.
    - `extractPage(doc)` = parse **once** → `analyzePage($, …)` over the untouched root → pre-clean the same `$` → `readArticle` → `classifyShape(…)` with the article's length. Analysis runs first because the pre-clean deletes `nav`, `aside`, `form`, and `script`, which hold pagination, facets, and JSON-LD.
    - `analyzePage` must not mutate `$`; a test asserts that `$.html()` is identical before and after.
    - Export `PageExtractor`.
  - **Links** (`links.ts`):
    - Resolve each `a[href]` and `link[rel~=next|prev]` against `<base href>` when present, else `doc.finalUrl`.
    - Keep only http/https. Drop `javascript:`, `data:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, fragment-only links, and same-document links (canonical URL equal to the page's).
    - Skip links inside `[hidden]` or `[aria-hidden="true"]`.
    - Dedupe by FEAT-050 `canonicalUrl`, keeping the first non-empty text.
    - Classify each link:
      - **`pagination`**, when any of these holds:
        1. it has `rel` next/prev;
        2. it is in a sibling group of at least 2 anchors whose texts are positive integers, and whose URLs differ from each other in exactly one query value or one numeric path segment;
        3. its accessible name is in `PAGINATION_WORDS` (next, previous, prev, older, newer, », ›, «, ‹; documented as generic vocabulary, with localization noted in TODO), and its URL is a variant of the page URL.
      - **`navigation`**, inside the landmarks listed in §2.
      - **`content`**, otherwise. `facet` and `record` are assigned in TASK-002.
    - Rank by kind (`pagination`, `facet`, `content`, `navigation`), then same-site first (`domainFromUrl` equality), then document order. Bound at `MAX_LINKS`, and count everything found per kind.
    - "Variant of the page URL" is one exported predicate, `isUrlVariant(page, candidate)`. It holds for the same origin when one of these holds:
      - the same path with an added or changed query;
      - the page path extended by exactly one segment;
      - the same path except the last segment.
  - **Shape skeleton** (`shape.ts`): this task emits `article` when Readability found an article, `index` when it did not but at least one non-`navigation` link exists, and otherwise "empty", which callers map to today's `EXTRACTION_EMPTY`. The remaining shapes arrive in TASK-002 through TASK-004.
  - **`readableText`**: the article text, or, when there is no article, `normalizeExtractedText(htmlToText(body))` computed from the pre-cleaned `$`. That is still the same parse.
  - **Boundary test** (`structural-only.spec.ts`): scan `src/extraction/page/**/*.ts` and fail on:
    - `attr('class')`, `attr('id')`, `.hasClass(`, `[class`, `[id`, `classList`, `className`;
    - any string literal that looks like a hostname (`/\b[a-z0-9-]+\.(com|net|org|io|co)\b/`);
    - any `SITE_TOKEN_SOURCE` match.

    Comments are exempt, matching the lint rule.

- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - **Goldens.** For every existing `__fixtures__` article (`article.html`, `wiki-refs.html`, `paywall.html`, `malformed.html`), `extractPage(doc).article` deep-equals `extract(doc)`, and `contentText` is byte-identical to a golden captured **before** the refactor.
  - **Parse count.** With a counting `parseHtml`: `extract` makes 1 parse and `extractPage` makes 1. The `JSDOM` construction count is 1 for both (spy on the injected window factory if one is needed).
  - **No mutation.** `$.html()` is unchanged by `analyzePage`.
  - **Links:**
    - relative and `<base>` resolution;
    - all four drop rules;
    - `aria-hidden` skip;
    - dedup across `…/x/` and `…/x#y`;
    - `rel=next` → pagination, and a `1 2 3 Next` group → pagination;
    - a footer link → navigation;
    - same-site ranking ahead of off-site;
    - a 120-link page → 40 shown and `found: 120`, with `by_kind` summing to `found`.
  - `isUrlVariant` table: query-changed, one segment longer, sibling segment, different origin (false), two segments longer (false).
  - **Shape:** a hub fixture with only links → `index`; an empty body → empty.
  - The boundary scan fails on a synthetic file containing `$(el).attr('class')` and passes on the real directory.

### TASK-002: Collection records and facet lists, including the G2 regression

- [ ] **Implementation** (`records.ts`), following plan §7 steps 1 to 4:
  1. **Candidates.** For each element with at least `MIN_RECORDS` element children (`tr` children are excluded; tables belong to TASK-004):
     - Compute each child's signature: its tag name plus the multiset of descendant tag names to depth 3. Class and id are never read.
     - Find the modal signature, and keep the children whose Jaccard similarity to it is at least `SIBLING_SIMILARITY`.
     - Of those, keep the children holding at least one `a[href]` and at least `RECORD_MIN_TEXT` visible characters.

     A container qualifies with at least `MIN_RECORDS` such children.

  2. **Score.** `count × log(1 + mean text length) × (1 + share with a link) × (1 + share with a numeric token)`, multiplied by `LANDMARK_PENALTY` inside a `nav`/`header`/`footer`/`aside` landmark or role.
     - **Facet list.** A candidate is a facet list, not a collection, when at least 60% of its items meet all three of these:
       - visible text of at most `FACET_LABEL_MAX` characters;
       - a count token (a parenthesized integer, or a trailing integer in its own element);
       - a link to an `isUrlVariant` of the page URL.

       Its links become `facet` links, and it never yields records.

     - The highest-scoring remaining candidate wins. When a winner's records each contain a qualifying inner container, the **outer** container wins, so cards rather than card fragments become records. Other qualifying regions are counted in `coverage.records` as `other_regions`.

  3. **Per record** (§2 `PageRecord`):
     - the title, the primary URL, and secondary links;
     - `segments` from block-level text runs, where anchor text counts as text. This is the G2 fix: the seller is a link, and it stays a segment;
     - `fields` from `dt`/`dd`, in-record `th`/`td`, and "Label: value" segments (a label of at most 5 words and `LABEL_MAX` characters);
     - `numbers`:
       - currency: `[$€£¥₹]` or a three-letter ISO code adjacent to a number;
       - distance: a number followed by `mi`, `miles`, `km`, or `kilometers`;
       - count: a parenthesized integer;
     - bounding at `RECORD_TEXT_CHARS` at a segment boundary;
     - `key` per §2.
  4. **Links.** A record's primary URL is kind `record` and is excluded from `links[]` (`recordLinkCount` counts them). Facet links are added to `links[]` and rank second, after pagination.
  - **Shape.** `collection` qualifies with at least `MIN_RECORDS` records. Arbitration against `article` is in TASK-004. Until then, `collection` wins whenever it qualifies.
  - Coverage: `records.{found, shown, with_link, with_fields}`. When `found > MAX_RECORDS`, `omitted` gets "N records beyond the first 25 were not shown". It adds "; pagination links are in links[]" only when `links[]` holds a pagination link. Advice names only engineered moves.

- [ ] **Unit Tests** (fixtures, each a generic pattern):
  - `listing-cards`: 6 cards, each with a heading link, a price, a "Seller name · 12.3 mi" line, and a detail link → `collection`, 6 records, each with title, url, a currency number, a distance number, and a seller segment.
  - **G2 regression**, `listing-card-linked-seller` (plan §9): price as plain text, title and seller as links → the record's segments contain the seller text, and its `links` contain the seller URL.
  - `facet-list`: a sidebar of "Label (44)" links to one-segment-longer URLs → 0 records from it and N `facet` links. A page holding both a facet list and cards → records come from the cards only.
  - `nested-cards`: cards whose inner spec list also repeats → records are the cards.
  - `nav-menu`: a 12-item `nav` list → no collection (landmark penalty plus short text).
  - `comment-thread`: an article with 10 short comments → TASK-004 asserts `article`. Here, records are found and scored.
  - Bounds: 60 cards → 25 shown and `found: 60`, with no pagination phrase unless a pagination link exists. A 2,000-character card → 400 characters with a whole-segment cut.
  - Determinism: two runs produce deep-equal output.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for research and agentic tasks (what a collection read returns).
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/extraction/page/records.spec.ts tests/extraction/page/structural-only.spec.ts` passes.

### TASK-003: Schema.org structured data (JSON-LD and microdata) as untrusted, bounded data

- [ ] **Implementation** (`structured.ts`):
  - **JSON-LD.** Read `script[type="application/ld+json"]` text up to `JSONLD_SCRIPT_BYTES` each and `JSONLD_TOTAL_BYTES` in total. `JSON.parse` only: never evaluated. A malformed block counts in `coverage.structured.malformed`, and is not swallowed silently.
    - Walk `@graph`, top-level arrays, and `ItemList.itemListElement[].item` (or the `ListItem` itself when it carries the item properties) up to `STRUCTURED_DEPTH`.
    - A node is an entity when any of its `@type` values is in `SCHEMA_TYPE_ALLOWLIST`.
  - **Microdata.** Read `[itemscope][itemtype]` elements whose type's last path segment is allowlisted. Collect `itemprop` values (`content`, `href`, `src`, `datetime`, or text). Nested `itemscope` elements become dotted properties.
  - **`SCHEMA_TYPE_ALLOWLIST`**:
    - the roots `Product`, `Offer`, `AggregateOffer`, `ItemList`, `Organization`, `Place`, `Event`;
    - a hand-maintained list of their schema.org subtypes (for example `Vehicle`, `Car`, `IndividualProduct`, `ProductModel`, `LocalBusiness` and its subtypes, `Accommodation`, `Residence`, and `Event` subtypes).

    A header comment cites schema.org as the vocabulary and says the list holds vocabulary names, not sites. A test asserts that every entry maps to one root through a small `SUBTYPE_OF` table kept beside it. Other types (`WebPage`, `BreadcrumbList`, `Article`, `WebSite`) are counted in `ignored_types`.

  - **Flattening.** Every scalar property is kept, with no per-vertical property list. Nested objects flatten to dotted keys up to depth 4. Arrays of scalars are joined with `, `. Arrays of objects are indexed (`offers.0.price`) up to 3 elements. Bounds are per §2. JSON-LD keywords other than `@type` (`@context`, `@id`) are dropped.
  - **Shape.** An `ItemList` holding at least `MIN_RECORDS` allowlisted entities, or at least `MIN_RECORDS` top-level entities sharing one root, qualifies the page as `collection` even with no DOM records (FEAT-049's `structured-listing`). When records and entities both exist, both are returned.
  - **URL properties.** Values that look like absolute http(s) URLs (`url`, `offers.url`, and the like) are returned as data. The agent records them as `discovered` with link kind `structured` when it shows them (TASK-006).
  - Replace `extractJsonLdDatePublished` with a call into the same JSON-LD reader, so JSON-LD is read by one grammar. The `publishedAt` result must be unchanged; the golden tests from TASK-001 pin it.

- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - `json-ld-itemlist`: an `ItemList` of 6 `Product`s, each with a nested `Offer` (`price`, `priceCurrency`, `seller.name`) and `color` → 6 entities with `offers.price`, `offers.seller.name`, and `color`, and shape `collection`.
  - `microdata-product`: one `Product` with a nested `Offer` → one entity with the same dotted keys.
  - Limits:
    - a 300 KiB script is skipped and counted;
    - depth-8 nesting is cut at depth 4 with no throw;
    - 80 entities → 25 shown;
    - a 5 KB description is cut to 300 characters.
  - A malformed block is counted, and the other blocks still parse.
  - `@type: ["Thing", "Product"]` is accepted, and `WebPage` is ignored and listed.
  - Security property test: a JSON-LD string holding `</script><script>…`, a `javascript:` URL, or a 10 MB repeat string is returned inert, bounded, and never evaluated. No global is touched.
  - Every allowlisted subtype resolves to a root.
  - `publishedAt` is unchanged on the article goldens.

### TASK-004: All tables, detail fields, and shape arbitration

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`tables.ts`.** Every `<table>` in document pre-order gets `index`.
    - `layout` is a table with one cell or a nested table, and it has no rows.
    - `key-value` is a table where at least 80% of rows have exactly 2 cells whose first cell is a `th` or at most `LABEL_MAX` characters.
    - Everything else is `data`.
    - Headers come from `thead th`, or from a first row made entirely of `th`.
    - Spans are not expanded (TODO). Bounds are per §2, and `coverage.tables.found` counts every table.
  - **`fields.ts`.** Page-level label/value pairs from:
    - `dl` pairs;
    - `key-value` table rows;
    - "Label: value" lines in visible text outside landmarks.

    Bounded at `MAX_FIELDS`, with a duplicate label+value pair kept once.

  - **`shape.ts` arbitration.** Compute visible-text mass for each qualifying candidate:
    - `collection`: records' text, or structured entities' serialized scalar text when the page has no DOM records.
    - `table`: the text of data tables with at least 3 data rows and at least 2 columns.
    - `detail`: field text, with at least 4 fields, **or** exactly one allowlisted non-`ItemList` main entity carrying at least 4 properties.
    - `article`: Readability's text length × `ARTICLE_MASS_WEIGHT`, weighted because Readability on a listing keeps fragments of every card.

    The winner has the largest mass. Ties break `collection` > `table` > `detail` > `article`. With no candidates, the TASK-001 rules apply (`index` or empty). `coverage.shape_basis` names the winner and the runner-up with both masses.

- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - `multi-table` pattern: a summary table followed by an answer table → `tables[1]` holds the answer cell, `tables[0].index === 0`, and shape `table`.
  - Nested layout table → `kind: 'layout'` with no rows, and the inner table still gets the next index.
  - `detail-attributes`: a product page with a 12-row key-value attribute table holding "Exterior color" and "Interior color" → `detail`, and `fields` contain both colors.
  - `article-with-infobox`: a 1,500-word article with a 10-row infobox → `article`, `text` byte-identical to `extract()`, and the infobox present in `fields` as a secondary part.
  - `comment-thread` (from TASK-002) → `article`.
  - The G2 listing (Readability returns about 2 KB of fragments; the cards hold about 5 KB) → `collection`, with a `shape_basis` naming both masses.
  - Every pre-existing article golden still classifies as `article`.
  - A 60-row table → 50 rows shown and `found` noted.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No credentials are involved. Browser snapshots come from the run's ephemeral profile.
- **Security**:
  - **Discovered links grant provenance only** (plan §6). They still pass the unchanged URL policy (length cap, https, credential-shape scan, host budget) and the ethics gate on use.
  - Links are bounded at 40, deduplicated, and stripped of `javascript:`, `data:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, and same-document targets. A link the sanitizer would alter is withheld rather than offered in a form that differs from what was recorded.
  - Every hop's audit names its `via` source, so an exfiltration chain is visible.
  - Hand-assembled URLs are now refused by `web_fetch` as well, which closes TODO 208's laundering path.
  - **Structured data is data** (plan §6). It is `JSON.parse`d only, bounded by bytes, depth, and count, and allowlisted by `@type`. Every string reaches the model through the same middleware sanitizer as page text, so phone and email redaction applies; business contact data stays redacted per plan §12 item 8.
  - **Challenge pages** are never analyzed on either path. `browser_extract` now applies FEAT-050's classifier before analysis.
  - **No site logic.** The structural-only boundary test, the extended `SITE_TOKEN_SOURCE`, and generic fixtures. `PAGINATION_WORDS`, the numeric-unit tokens, and the schema.org allowlist are documented generic vocabulary, in the same category as ARIA roles.
- **Error Handling**:
  - Extraction never throws for page content. Malformed JSON-LD, broken tables, and truncated snapshots become coverage facts, never a swallowed `catch {}`. Every catch in `extraction/page/` either counts into coverage or rethrows (memory → never silently swallow errors).
  - Readability's existing null-on-failure contract is unchanged.
  - New and updated tool messages are registered templates that declare their capability: `unattested-fetch-url`, `page-summary`, `table-index`, `extraction-kind`, `EXTRACTION_EMPTY`, and the `omitted` phrases. Advice names only moves the engine supports: `web_search` (including `limit: 0`), `web_fetch` of an offered URL, `browser_extract` kinds, and following an offered link.
- **Logging**: There are no new log lines, because shape and coverage travel in tool results and `tool-calls.jsonl`. `RunHealth.extraction` and the `run_health` event summarize counts with no URLs or page text. Audit `provenance` details carry the `S<n>` source ID and the link kind, never page text.
- **Diagnostic cost**:
  - Analysis reuses the extractor's single cheerio parse; the parse counter asserts 0 extra parses.
  - Deterministic `ask` and `research` call `extract()`, which runs no analysis.
  - `browser_extract` takes one `evaluate` per call.
  - The challenge classifier's cheap pass parses nothing on a page with no challenge marker (FEAT-050's spy test).
- **Compatibility**:
  - Article `text` is byte-identical.
  - `RunHealth.extraction` is optional, and old run directories validate.
  - Tool payloads change shape, which the internal pre-release contracts allow.
  - `UrlProvenance.record` requiring an origin is an internal clean break.
  - No user-owned artifact format changes.
- **Enhancement tracking** (appended to `.spec-lite/TODO.md` with this spec):
  - A store-served continuation (`records_offset`) for pages with more than 25 records.
  - Localizing `PAGINATION_WORDS`.
  - RDFa structured data.
  - Expanding `rowspan`/`colspan` in tables.
  - Offering links withheld because the sanitizer would alter them (for example a path containing a masked user value).
  - Using the shape-aware view for the `browser_observe` digest (related to TODO line 209).
